newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthening on dollar surplus.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthening on dollar surplus.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling continued firm against the dollar on a strong dollar surplus amid poor demand, commercial bank dealers said on Tuesday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.41 against the dollar compared to 54.48 on Monday. Against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 88.25 from 88.71.
"Market sentiment for a stronger shilling is very strong," a dealer said.
Dealers said despite reports that the strengthening shilling was hurting exporters, basic market fundamentals were the main thrust behind the shilling's bull.

"Demand is very very low, while inflows from agriculture, tourism and foreign investors are flowing in steadily," one dealer said. The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted below 10 percent unchanged.
